relationships.subject: epithelial basement membrane dystrophy
relationships.evidence_quote: Displaced basement membrane separates basal cells from their usual substrate and disrupts hemidesmosomal anchoring, leaving epithelium vulnerable to lid-induced shear and recurrent erosion

relationships.subject: alpha6beta4 integrin
relationships.evidence_quote: Basal epithelial hemidesmosomes, including α6β4 integrin and collagen XVII, bind laminin-332

relationships.subject: MMP-3
relationships.evidence_quote: MMP-3 (stromelysin-1) degrades multiple extracellular matrix components, including laminin, nidogen, perlecan, and collagen IV

relationships.subject: TGF-beta
relationships.evidence_quote: When the EBM fails to regenerate after epithelial-stromal injury, persistent growth-factor entry promotes development and survival of opacity-producing anterior stromal myofibroblasts

relationships.subject: epithelial basement membrane
relationships.evidence_quote: Collagen IV, perlecan, and nidogens help restrict stromal access to epithelial- and tear-derived transforming growth factor β (TGF-β) and platelet-derived growth factor (PDGF)

key_findings: Narrative review: EBMD predisposes to recurrent corneal erosions through disorganized multilaminar basement membrane that disrupts hemidesmosomal anchoring.

Treatment choice (lubrication, bandage lenses, debridement, keratectomy, PTK, stromal puncture) depends on the goal (pain control, recurrence prevention, visual rehabilitation); no technique is universally superior and MMP roles remain unestablished.
